bull.b: Strong growth across total revenue and e-commerce indicates improving product adoption and distribution reach. In-house channel management and rising online demand could support repeat purchases and a broader customer base over the coming quarters.

Higher gross margins, supported by channel mix, direct sales economics, pricing discipline and raw-material costs, improve the potential for operating leverage. Sustained margin quality would help the company convert revenue growth into better cash generation.

Subscription growth can create recurring demand and improve customer retention compared with one-time product purchases. Expanding subscribers also gives SenesTech a more predictable revenue base and a direct relationship with end users.

bear.b: Large continuing losses show that the current revenue base does not yet cover operating costs, despite improved gross margins. Without substantial scale or expense reductions, profitability remains uncertain and the company may need further financing.

bear.t: Cash Burn and Limited Liquidity Runway
bear.b: Material cash consumption and a limited runway constrain strategic flexibility. If revenue growth or cost control falls short, SenesTech could require additional capital, potentially increasing dilution or limiting investment in sales and product development.

The company’s longer-term growth case depends partly on converting trials and targeted vertical activity into repeatable institutional contracts. Delayed approvals and unclear timing for large wins make future revenue scale and customer diversification difficult to assess.
